topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how exposure associations and population patterns inform the debate over environmental contributions to cancer.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of interacting infectious influences.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations through processes shaped by cellular metabolism and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation initiation from the growth-promoting conditions that allow initiated cells to develop into tumours.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposure influences carcinogenic effects and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure through mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how patterns in cancer genomes can provide retrospective evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of carcinogenicity assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential is assessed and why available approaches cannot fully reproduce human cancer development.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions and frames their practical significance as everyday risk–benefit decisions.
